title: Basin-scale underwater positioning without surfacing

concept.text: The innovation is a positioning service that lets submerged mobile platforms determine where they are across an ocean basin, over thousands of kilometers and for weeks, without surfacing for a GPS fix. Its defining capability is sustained coverage with a scientifically useful, predefined error bound. The concept is independent of the transmission channel; long-range acoustic navigation is the approach developed in the supplied sources.

GPS signals cannot penetrate seawater sufficiently to provide submerged positioning. Acoustic signals can travel long distances underwater, but their travel times depend on the propagation path, the changing sound-speed field and timing errors. A positioning system must convert those measurements into locations while accounting for these effects. Acoustic travel time is therefore a usable ranging measurement that requires corrections, rather than a direct distance ruler with a fixed conversion.

significance.text: Reliable basin-wide positioning would remove a major constraint on autonomous oceanography, particularly under ice, where surfacing may be impossible. Its direct scientific benefits would include better georeferencing of observations and a stronger basis for combining measurements from different mobile platforms in ocean data assimilation. Where the navigation architecture requires it, low-rate information could support environmental and timing corrections.

Impact synthesis: sustained positioning could substantially expand long-duration autonomous surveys and make repeated observations across remote ocean regions more practical. Making such work routine would also require sufficient vehicle endurance, reliability, communications, deployment infrastructure and affordable operation. Positioning would enable those missions; it would not by itself supply all the capabilities needed to conduct them.

The analogy to underwater GPS describes the user benefit of obtaining positions without surfacing. It does not establish that an acoustic system would match satellite GPS in accuracy, update rate, availability or infrastructure requirements. Local acoustic positioning and regional navigation demonstrations are important foundations; the proposed advance is their extension into a sustained basin-wide service with specified performance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability identified by this record is an integrated service that maintains bounded position errors across a basin and over weeks without requiring surface GPS fixes. Detecting a signal, decoding a waveform or estimating a platform position on one regional trajectory demonstrates part of that capability. The complete service must maintain useful positions across its declared operating domain, with specified update intervals and availability.

For an acoustic implementation, the central scientific barrier is separating position-dependent travel time from changes in propagation. Temperature, salinity and ocean variability alter sound speed and bend propagation paths; internal waves also scatter signals. Howe and coauthors explain that positioning at the scale of tens of meters requires accounting for sound-speed changes in both space and time. Clock drift and synchronization errors introduce additional timing uncertainty. Joint estimation of position and sound speed offers a route forward, but also couples the navigation problem to knowledge of the ocean environment.

Engineering synthesis: a practical system must integrate signal reception, timing, environmental corrections, source geometry and onboard position estimation so that their combined errors remain within the declared bound. It must also characterize outages and degraded performance across different depths, locations and ocean conditions. A non-acoustic approach could satisfy the same positioning objective, but would need to demonstrate equivalent service performance through its own measurement and error-control mechanisms.

current_state.text: The retained DARPA POSYDON page describes a program intended to provide robust positioning across ocean basins using long-range acoustic sources, allowing underwater platforms to obtain positions without surfacing. It states that the program is complete and that the page is no longer maintained. The page supplies no achieved accuracy, coverage or operational deployment result. Program completion therefore establishes the program's administrative status, rather than successful deployment of the proposed service.

Howe and coauthors' 2019 review documents achieved components and a future multipurpose acoustic-network vision. It reports approximately 80 m RMS estimated glider position errors over ranges of 700 km in the 2010–2011 Philippine Sea experiment. Those results involved time synchronization using GPS at the surface and subsequent analysis. They demonstrate useful regional acoustic navigation capability, but do not establish continuous onboard positioning across an ocean basin for a month without surfacing. The review also recommends bringing multipurpose acoustic observing systems to operational status; that is a historical recommendation, not evidence of their operational status in 2026.

The research notes attribute a roughly 3,500 km Kauai–Wake digital-symbol demonstration to Gemba, Durofchalk, Allen, Bush and Edelmann in JASA Express Letters 6, article 108401, dated 26 October 2026. They describe it as a waveform and modulation demonstration rather than a complete navigation trial. However, no retained text or source artifact accompanies the cited DOI, so the supplied review could not verify the paper's identity, authorship, date, distance or characterization. The notes report an earlier publisher-text retrieval followed by a failed direct refetch, but that access history is not independently documented. The reported result remains an unverified component claim in this record, rather than evidence of a completed positioning service; the missing artifact does not establish that the result is false.

The same unretained publisher material is reported to relate a 34 ms travel-time error to about 50 m of range at a sound speed of 1,480 m/s. Arithmetic alone gives 0.034 × 1,480 = 50.32 m, but it does not verify the reported experimental error. A range-equivalent timing error also does not establish an equal position error: position accuracy depends on the measurement geometry and the other contributors to the error budget.

Evidence-scope conclusion: the retained sources document local and regional capabilities, a basin-scale program objective and a proposed network architecture. They do not document an operational civilian basin-wide service. The supplied freshness record is empty, so this evidence cannot establish that no such service existed as of 1 November 2026. The unmaintained POSYDON page also cannot rule out later or undisclosed results. Present operational status, deployment feasibility and timeline remain unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: multiple mobile platforms obtain onboard positions within 100 m, or another scientifically justified bound fixed in advance, for 30 days without surfacing, across a predefined operating domain spanning one ocean basin. Specify the horizontal and vertical error requirements, error statistic, depths, update intervals, availability and permitted external assistance before the trial. The 100 m tolerance and 30-day duration are proposed targets, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Multiple platforms sustain predefined basin-scale accuracy submerged for 30 days

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: measure errors throughout the trial using independent reference observations or an independently validated reference trajectory. Include a final independent fix as an additional closure check. An endpoint fix alone cannot establish that the error bound held during the preceding month, because intermediate errors may grow and later cancel. Assess positions available to the platforms during operation separately from estimates improved through subsequent analysis.
completion_criteria.label: Independent references validate onboard positioning errors throughout the trial

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: repeat trials across representative locations, depths and changing ocean conditions; report outages, uncertainty estimates, infrastructure requirements and the full error budget. Make sufficient methods, calibration information and evaluation data available for independent assessment and replication. A waveform test over one path would remain a component demonstration. Successful finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested domain and conditions, rather than literal coverage of every point or every possible ocean state.
completion_criteria.label: Repeated trials establish reproducibility and report practical positioning limits

related_concepts.text: OCE-02, Synoptic sensing of the ocean interior: positioning determines where a platform is, while synoptic sensing measures the ocean's interior state. Acoustic navigation and tomography can share sources, timing information and sound-speed estimation, and Howe and coauthors describe joint position and sound-speed estimation. This is a documented technical overlap, but successful positioning alone would not establish synoptic climate-state measurement.

Roster-based distinction: OCE-08, Continuous centimeter-level geodesy of the seismogenic seafloor, concerns tectonic displacement at a much finer stated measurement scale. OCE-10 concerns the locations of mobile submerged platforms over basin distances. The supplied evidence does not establish that the same sound-speed limitation governs both concepts or that solving either would solve the other. A non-acoustic positioning solution could satisfy OCE-10 without resolving OCE-02 or OCE-08.

Roster-based synthesis: OCE-04, Persistent mobile operations at full ocean depth, overlaps through the needs of autonomous vehicles. Basin-wide positioning could support those operations, but it does not establish full-depth endurance, pressure tolerance or persistent operation. Conversely, a vehicle capable of persistent full-depth work would still need an adequate navigation solution for its mission.

Roster-based synthesis: OCE-01, A closed theory of oceanic turbulent transport, and OCE-06, A verified law of ice-shelf basal melting, concern physical processes that mobile observations could help investigate. Under-ice positioning could support ice-shelf observations, while better environmental knowledge could inform acoustic navigation. Neither process law follows from obtaining platform positions.

Roster-based synthesis: OCE-03, A predictive closure of the biological carbon pump; OCE-05, Closure of ocean–crust fluid and biogeochemical exchange; OCE-07, The stability class of the global overturning circulation; and OCE-09, A predictive theory of pelagic size structure and trophic transfer, could benefit from better-located autonomous observations. Their missing capabilities concern biogeochemical budgets, exchange processes, circulation stability or ecological prediction. Navigation infrastructure would support data collection without supplying those scientific closures. Each remains a distinct innovation alongside OCE-10.

unresolved_issues: The cited Gemba and coauthors paper lacks retained text. Its bibliographic identity, reported 3,500 km demonstration, navigation-trial distinction and 34 ms error remain unverified.
The empty freshness record leaves operational civilian basin-scale service status as of 1 November 2026 unresolved; undisclosed results also cannot be assessed.
The final operating domain, scientifically justified accuracy bound, error statistic, update interval, availability and depth requirements remain to be specified.
A practical method for independent validation throughout a month-long basin-scale submerged trial has not been established by the supplied material.
The supplied sources do not establish the proposed technical benefit to OCE-08; detailed OCE-02 and OCE-08 materials were not included.
Deployment feasibility, infrastructure cost and timeline remain unresolved. No substantive review recommendation was rejected.

brief.title: Knowing where you are underwater without surfacing
possible: Ocean robots could know where they are across an entire ocean basin for weeks without coming to the surface. Their position errors would stay within a limit chosen for the scientific mission, even beneath ice that prevents surfacing.
why: Scientists could run longer autonomous surveys and return more readily to remote ocean regions. Knowing where each observation was made would also help them combine measurements from different robots into a clearer picture of the ocean.

sources.showed: Their review reports estimated underwater glider position errors of about 80 metres in a regional experiment. The analysis used surface GPS timing and calculations made afterward.
sources.quote: Acoustic receivers are now routinely acquiring data on a global scale, e.g., Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization International Monitoring System hydroacoustic arrays, various regional integrated ocean observing systems, and some profiling floats.
sources.cited_for: Sound-based ocean observing systems and regional navigation provide foundations for a wider positioning network.
sources.not_established: The regional experiment did not establish sustained onboard positioning across an ocean basin without surfacing.

sources.showed: DARPA's POSYDON program pursued continuous underwater positioning across ocean basins using distant sound sources. Its program summary reports no achieved positioning performance.
sources.cited_for: A basin-wide positioning system using long-range sound sources has been a concrete research objective.
sources.not_established: Completion of the program does not establish that the proposed service achieved its accuracy or coverage goals.

sources.who: Gemba, Durofchalk, Allen, Bush and Edelmann
sources.showed: This is a reported test of sending digitally encoded signals over a long underwater path.
sources.cited_for: The work concerns long-range underwater signaling as a component of navigation.
sources.not_established: A signal transmission test does not establish accurate positions or a sustained positioning service.

shown: Regional navigation is the strongest demonstrated foundation described by Howe and colleagues. Extending it across a basin requires separating changes in location from changes in how sound travels through the ocean. Temperature, salinity and drifting clocks can all alter the measured travel time.
missing: An integrated system still needs to demonstrate sustained positions within a predefined error limit across its intended basin-wide operating area.
Independent measurements must establish how accurate the positions remain throughout a long submerged trial.
Repeated trials must establish when service fails or degrades across different depths, locations and ocean conditions.

milestones.label: Multiple vehicles maintain basin-wide accuracy for a month
milestones.explanation: Multiple vehicles would have to calculate positions onboard across a defined ocean basin for 30 days without surfacing, meeting accuracy and service limits set beforehand. This would establish sustained positioning.

milestones.label: Independent measurements confirm accuracy throughout the trial
milestones.explanation: Independent references would have to validate positions available onboard throughout the trial, with a final fix as an extra check. This would reveal intermediate errors that could cancel before the end.

milestones.label: Repeated trials establish reliability and practical limits
milestones.explanation: Repeated trials would have to report errors, outages and infrastructure needs across varied conditions, with enough methods and data for independent assessment. This would establish reproducibility and the limits of demonstrated coverage.

uncertain: The scientifically useful accuracy limit, depth range, update frequency and acceptable availability remain to be defined.
A practical way to obtain independent reference positions throughout a month-long submerged basin trial remains unresolved.
Deployment feasibility, infrastructure costs and the time needed to build a practical service remain uncertain.

page.title: Basin-scale underwater acoustic positioning
page.definition: Submerged vehicles determine their geographic positions in real time across an ocean basin from distant sound sources, without surfacing for satellite navigation. Acoustic travel times—the delays between transmission and reception—provide the ranging measurements.

goal.need: In the 2010–2011 Philippine Sea experiment, four Seagliders recorded acoustic signals at ranges up to 700 km; incorporating their travel times reduced estimated underwater position errors as shown below. Clock synchronization used GPS at the surface. Eliminating surface visits for navigation is DARPA's basin-scale positioning objective.

figures.caption: Estimated underwater position errors for four Seagliders in the 2010–2011 Philippine Sea experiment
figures.note: The acoustic positions were calculated in subsequent analysis; the gliders synchronized their clocks using surface GPS.

statements.quote: seeks to develop an undersea, ocean basin-scale, PNT system
statements.context: The POSYDON solicitation describes its objective; PNT means positioning, navigation and timing.

statements.quote: This system aims to enhance the U.S. Navy's ability to provide precise, global positioning throughout the ocean basins.

completion.title: An integrated system passes government validation of basin-scale underwater acoustic positioning.
completion.criterion: An integrated acoustic system demonstrates real-time positioning across an ocean basin without the receiving platform surfacing for GPS, with all POSYDON components validated by the government team. Programme success is assessed against metrics covering position accuracy, depth, operating range, jamming resistance and navigation sensor-suite power. Their numerical values are in a classified addendum and cannot be reproduced from the public solicitation.
completion.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-30, sections 1.2–1.4: the proposed Phase III integrated demonstration and programme success metrics.
completion.basis: This is POSYDON's culminating system test. DARPA marks the programme complete, and BAE reports completing its final stages, but neither source publishes acceptance measurements. BAE's statement is not peer reviewed. Achievement against the classified metrics remains publicly unverified.

milestones.title: Underwater acoustic positioning components work together in a laboratory prototype.
milestones.criterion: Integrate the basic hardware components of an underwater acoustic positioning technology and validate their operation together in a laboratory prototype. This applies the Department of Defense's technology readiness level 4 criterion; it does not assign a readiness rating to POSYDON.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Defense, Technology Readiness Assessment Guidebook, Table 2-1, technology readiness level 4; a general hardware maturity criterion, not a POSYDON-specific gate.
milestones.threshold_quote: Basic technological components are integrated to establish that they will work together.

milestones.title: At-sea observations validate acoustic measurement models and establish signal availability.
milestones.criterion: Validate acoustic measurement models and assess signal availability using observations spanning shipping channels, deep ocean and continental shelves. Phase I permits subsequent processing. The Philippine Sea glider results provide regional evidence; their surface clock synchronization and subsequent analysis do not demonstrate continuous onboard basin-scale positioning.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-30, sections 1.2 and 1.3.1.3, Phase I at-sea validation.

milestones.title: An underwater acoustic system demonstrates ranging in real time.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate acoustic range estimation in real time, the POSYDON Phase II result preceding integrated positioning. The public programme summary supplies no measured ranging error, demonstration range or sample size against this gate.
milestones.threshold_quote: demonstrating a real-time acoustic ranging capability

results.finding: One integrated underwater positioning prototype achieved above 70% accuracy on both axes within 500–1000 mm.
results.detail: The prototype combined acoustic modems, an IMU and a depth sensor in a 2 m water tank. The number of trajectory measurements was not stated. Tank-wall reflections and IMU drift contributed to variability.
results.quote:
The system maintains reliable performance at ranges between 
500–1000 mm, with accuracy rates above 70% for both axes.

results.finding: Kauai Beacon signals were received at 8 of 11 ocean observatory hydrophone locations.
results.detail: Simulations with internal waves reproduced observed arrivals at most locations, though the Oregon Offshore reception differed from predictions. The text does not establish observations spanning shipping channels, deep ocean, and continental shelves.
results.quote: Positive receptions are reported at eight of the 11 hydrophone locations.

results.finding: Philippine Sea gliders: 93% of 1,727 automated range estimates agreed with manual estimates within 75 m.
results.detail: The deep-water observations provide regional evidence for acoustic arrival modeling and reception, but do not span shipping channels and continental shelves. Agreement is with manual processing of the same data, rather than an independent range measurement.
results.quote:
Compared to ranging results obtained by manual acoustic arrival matching, 93% of the automatically-obtained
range estimates were within 75 m of the manually-obtained range estimates.

results.finding: 2700 transmissions over a 3500 km acoustic path yielded mean channel capacity of 0.028 bits/(s Hz).
results.detail: Measurements at a moored receiver provide basin-scale telemetry evidence over 1.5 years. The source does not report travel-time measurement model validation or observations spanning shipping channels, deep ocean, and continental shelves.
results.quote: Analysis of 2700 M-sequence transmissions from Kauai to receiver H11S2 near Wake Island over a 1.5 yr duration and a nominal 3500 km distance yields a mean channel capacity of 0.028 bits/(s Hz).

results.finding: Beaufort Sea acoustic beacon ranging, sample size not stated: mean real-time absolute range error was roughly 11 m.
results.detail: The beacon transmissions were evaluated at distances up to 3 km. The real-time method consistently overestimated range.
results.quote: The mean real-time absolute range error between beacons is roughly 11 m at distances up to 3 km.

results.finding: 35 Hz signals were received by LPD-equipped platforms more than 550 km from the sources; platform count not stated.
results.detail: The Beaufort Sea observations provide regional evidence of signal availability. They do not validate measurement models or establish availability across shipping channels, deep ocean and continental shelves.
results.quote:

results.finding: A tank-tested acoustic localization system sent 102 ranging requests per run at 3.5-second intervals.
results.detail: The system used two-way acoustic ranging for localization in a 2 m water tank. It was not the POSYDON Phase II demonstration.
results.quote: Every run lasted approximately 6 min; 102 ranging requests were sent with an interval of 3.5 s using the acoustic modem.

results.finding: For 1,727 receptions used in positioning, 93% of automated range estimates were within 75 m of manual estimates.
results.detail: The algorithm was applied to previously collected recordings. Processing took less than 5 seconds for a typical reception on the stated computer, but real-time ranging was not demonstrated.
results.quote:
Of the automatically-obtained range estimates used
for vehicle positioning, 93% were within 75 m of the cor-
responding manually-obtained range estimates.

results.finding: Beaufort Sea beacon transmissions: mean real-time absolute range error was roughly 11 m; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The at-sea measurements evaluate an acoustic ranging model in one ice-covered region. They do not establish signal availability across shipping channels, deep ocean and continental shelves.
results.quote: The mean real-time absolute range error between beacons is roughly 11 m at distances up to 3 km.
